My dear [Mr Macmillan](/person/939),
I think I ought to refer to you a request I have had from Dr and Mrs Vaughan[^1] for leave to put two of the stories in [Golden Deeds](/book/51) i.e. 'The last fight in the Colyseum', and the faithful slaves of Haïti into a [Unknown Reference 392]book of readings] for National Schools acknowledging where they come from, but I conclude that you have no objection.

When there is a reprint, I have another faithful slave to put in who maintained his mistress by hair dressing in New York.

Thank you for the [Clever Woman](/book/58)’s arrival.

She looks very well and attractive, but I am prepared for all the critics doubting her reformation

Yours sincerely

C M Yonge


[^1]: Probably the Rev. [Charles John Vaughan](/person/1439) (1816-1897), vicar of Doncaster and former headmaster of Harrow School, and his wife Catherine Maria (Stanley) Vaughan (1821-1899).

Mrs Vaughan edited An Advanced Reading Book for Girls (1866).
